text:
The estate can recover the full damages flowing from the driver's negligence, including wrongful-death and survival damages (medical expenses, pain and suffering, lost earnings or support). The driver takes the victim as found, and a refusal of treatment grounded in religious belief is generally not an unreasonable failure to mitigate or a superseding cause. So the driver can't reduce liability on the ground that the pedestrian should have accepted the transfusion.

CONFIDENCE: 80
